summary: The Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships (GOI-IES) fund 60 high-calibre students from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK for one year of master's or doctoral study in Ireland, with a stipend and a full fee waiver.
covers: A €10,000 stipend for one year of full-time study.
A full tuition-fee waiver from your Irish host institution for the year of the scholarship.
eligibility: A domicile of origin outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK.
A conditional or final offer for a master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD (NFQ level 9 or 10) at an eligible Irish higher-education institution.
Russian and Belarusian nationals are not eligible, and previous GOI-IES holders cannot reapply.
how_to_apply: Apply to your Irish programme early so you hold an offer when the call opens.
Submit the GOI-IES application on the Higher Education Authority's online portal. The 2026 call closed at 5 pm Irish time on 12 March 2026; calls usually open in January.
Include your offer letter, transcripts, CV and personal statement, and upload two references yourself through the portal.
Results are usually announced in early June.
watch_out: The award funds one year only — for a multi-year PhD it covers the first year.
A €10,000 stipend will not cover a full year of Irish living costs; budget the difference.
You need a university offer before you apply, so start your admission applications in the autumn.

faq.q: What does the selection panel look for?
faq.a: Your academic record, your communication skills, your activities outside study, and a strong reason for choosing Ireland that fits your long-term goals.

faq.q: Can I apply more than once?
faq.a: One application per cycle, and anyone who has already held a GOI-IES scholarship cannot apply again.
Calls usually open in January. The 2026 call closed on 12 March 2026, with results in early June — so secure your Irish offer in the autumn before.
